intent: Add the spring-refresh exit mode and train from the CLI
end Spring runs by themselves and wire training into the CLI

title: end a Spring run with -Dspring.context.exit=onRefresh
why: Spring then exits with status 0 as soon as the application context has refreshed, so the tool needs no probing and no signal (PR 28). The limit is stated in the code and the README: only the startup path is trained, not classes first loaded while serving requests.
alternative: Poll an HTTP endpoint. That became the separate http-probe mode in issue 6.

title: describe a way to end a run as an ExitMode and check it against the application kind
why: An ExitMode supplies JVM arguments and a ReadyCondition and says which kinds of application it supports. AppTrainer rejects an unsupported pair before anything starts (PR 28). The interface is where issue 6 adds http-probe.

title: use exit codes 0 for success, 1 for a failed training run and 2 for invalid input
why: Inferred from the code and the PR text: invalid options and a failed run are different situations, and scripts can then tell them apart. The PR states the codes but does not give a reason.

title: reject non-Spring JARs for spring-refresh until http-probe exists
why: The mode only works with Spring, so a plain executable JAR gets a clear message that names the mode (PR 28). The PR says issue 6 will give those JARs a way to be trained.
alternative: Run it anyway and let it wait for an exit that never comes.

name: SpringRefreshExitMode
role: Adds -Dspring.context.exit=onRefresh and waits for the application to exit by itself
conditions: Spring Boot JARs only; trains the startup path only

name: ExitMode
role: Interface for how a run ends: JVM arguments, a ReadyCondition, the supported application kinds, and name parsing

name: AppTrainer
role: Combines the extracted application, the JDK, the strategy and an ExitMode into a trained archive
conditions: Rejects an unsupported mode and application pair before anything runs

subject: Not seen on a real Spring Boot application
why: PR 28 says that a real Spring application exiting with status 0 after onRefresh with a cache flag set was not observed, because no demo app could be built. A test app that exits only when it receives the property stands in for it. An opt-in test with a real JAR can check it.
